name: Half-Kneeling Cable High Row
summary: A unilateral pulling exercise performed from a half-kneeling stance that targets the latissimus dorsi and upper back through a diagonal high-to-low pulling path.

setup: Set a cable pulley to a high setting and attach a single D-handle.
Assume a half-kneeling position facing the machine, resting the knee on the working side on the floor and planting the opposite foot flat in front with the knee bent at ninety degrees.
Grasp the handle with the working hand using a neutral grip, and allow the cable tension to extend your arm forward and upward to stretch the lat while keeping your torso upright and braced.
steps: Initiate the pull by depressing your shoulder blade and driving your elbow down and back toward your hip.
Pull the handle down smoothly until your elbow is tight against your side, squeezing your lat at the end of the range of motion.
Pause briefly at peak contraction without twisting your torso.
Slowly extend your arm along the same diagonal path to return the weight stack, allowing the shoulder blade to upwardly rotate and stretch the lat.
Complete all prescribed repetitions on one side before switching knee and hand positions to work the opposite side.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull your elbow down toward your hip, and inhale as you return the handle to the overhead starting position.
cues: Drive your elbow into your back pocket.
Lead with the elbow, not the hand.
Keep your ribs down and torso squared.

common_faults.fault: Rotating the torso to assist in pulling the load.
common_faults.correction: Brace your abdominals and glutes to keep your shoulders and hips square throughout the repetition.

common_faults.fault: Initiating the pull with the bicep rather than the back.
common_faults.correction: Depress the shoulder blade first and focus on elbow drive rather than curling the wrist or forearm.

common_faults.fault: Arching the lower back excessively at the bottom of the pull.
common_faults.correction: Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg and engage your core to maintain a neutral spine.

precautions: Use a foam pad or exercise mat under the down knee to prevent joint discomfort.
